results.fact: The job-scoped worker claims the agent task and each evaluator task of its job
A job-scoped worker exits by itself with code 0 when its job ends
A worker in token mode gets the Kitaru secrets of the agent version
The agent process has a task token, and no key, worker ID or channel secret in its environment
A judge with the provider `openai` and a connection schema gets `OPENAI_API_KEY` from a default connection, in a job-scoped worker that holds no key
An evaluator with an inline dependency block (`openai==3.49.0`) installs and runs when root owns `/app`
The agent and the evaluators start when root owns all of `/app`, `.venv` included, with a source tree that cannot be written and a new `HOME` for each worker
Agent code can read the worker token from `/proc` of the worker
Agent code can read the channel secret from `/proc` of the process that started the worker
`python -m kitaru.worker` with `KITARU_WORKER_TIMEOUT`, in token mode
The files of uid 1000 that stay after two Runs (the private directories are deleted, as the Supervisor does)
Each Replay of the two Runs completed and gave its report
Marker files of an earlier Replay that a Replay of the second Run finds
With the block, agent code cannot write `/tmp`, `/var/tmp`, `/run/lock` and `/home/kitaru`, and finds no marker there
No file stays in a private directory after its worker process exits
A Replay can list the private directories of the Replays that run at the same time (one uid)
10 `uv run` commands at the same time are safe on one cold uv cache (the command form of Kitaru)
A Run with 10 jobs completes with 10 job-scoped workers in one container and one shared uv cache
Peak memory of the container for the 10 workers (cgroup `memory.peak`, a local number, not Fargate)
A worker that gets SIGTERM one time drains: the agent task completes and the agent gets no signal
